mechanism_relevant_findings: The proposed mechanism of nanofluidic salt trapping explains the high pressures required to damage concrete under freeze-thaw conditions.
Ice nucleation in confined porous media leads to significant disjoining pressures due to trapped ions.
Surface ion condensation or solid salt precipitation occurs at lower temperatures to release pressure, allowing complete freezing.

numerical_findings.conditions: high pressure required to damage concrete

limitations: The applicability of previous frost heave theories to hardened cement is questionable due to its much higher stiffness.

relevance_judgement.reason: The paper presents a novel mechanism relevant to proton transport in the context of freeze-thaw damage in porous media.

trace_spans.section: Freezing point depression and freeze-thaw damage by nanofluidic salt trapping
